prompt:
This is a large, multi-module Android project. Somewhere in it there's a module responsible for persisting user preferences locally on-device (backed by a DataStore-based data source), with its own unit tests. Can you find that module, confirm its unit tests genuinely pass, and check whether its own source code leaves no more than 50 lines uncovered by those tests? Once you know the result, end your reply with a block in exactly this format (substitute the real module path, outcome, and numbers you found; keep the two marker lines exactly as shown, with valid JSON in between):

KMP_EVAL_RESULT
{"module": "<the Gradle module path you tested>", "outcome_kind": "coverage_threshold_exceeded", "total": <integer>, "passed": <integer>, "failed": <integer>, "missed_lines": <integer>, "threshold": <integer>, "modules_contributing": <integer>}
KMP_EVAL_RESULT_END

If its tests genuinely pass AND it stays within the 50-line budget, use {"module": "<the Gradle module path you tested>", "outcome_kind": "tests_executed", "total": <integer>, "passed": <integer>, "failed": <integer>} instead (omit the coverage fields). If some of its tests actually fail, use {"module": "<the Gradle module path you tested>", "outcome_kind": "tests_failed", "total": <integer>, "passed": <integer>, "failed": <integer>}. If the module turns out to have no applicable tests, use {"module": "<the Gradle module path you tested>", "outcome_kind": "no_applicable_tests"} (omit total/passed/failed).
expected_outcome: The agent discovers NowInAndroid's :core:datastore module, confirms its 14 unit tests pass cleanly, discovers it leaves 76 lines uncovered (exceeding a 50-line budget), and reports outcome_kind coverage_threshold_exceeded with the accurate missed_lines/threshold/modules_contributing.

first_useful_signal_predicate.description: first well-formed kmp_test evidence confirming :core:datastore's coverage gate fired at 76 missed lines > 50
